page: OVHcloud t1-180 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud instance configured with four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs providing a combined 64 GB of VRAM. It features 36 physical x86_64 cores across Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processors running at 3.0 GHz without hyperthreading, alongside 180.0 GB of system memory, 4050 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and a 10 Gbps network baseline. The system operates on the KVM hypervisor with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmark outcomes show distinct performance profiles across compute layers. The quadruple V100 GPU array achieves top-tier results in small and medium large language model inference, delivering 1,223.13 tokens per second in prompt processing and 111.59 tokens per second in text generation on 7B models. In contrast, the Intel Xeon Silver 4214 CPUs exhibit weak to poor single-core execution metrics, as shown in low single-threaded compression and Geekbench single-core scores, while multi-core metrics settle into mid-tier averages.

Hardware tradeoffs center on the balance between accelerator capability and host CPU throughput. While the GPU configuration and 4050 GB NVMe storage pool support high-throughput data ingestion and model execution, CPU-bound pre-processing tasks may experience bottlenecks from modest per-core performance. The architecture provides high resource density for parallel tasks, offering qualitative cost efficiency for multi-GPU training and inference workloads compared to modern flagship architectures, provided execution pipelines maximize GPU offload.

OVHcloud t1-180 is best suited for parallelized machine learning workloads, including medium-scale model inference, deep learning model training, computer vision, static web caching, and high-throughput data processing pipelines requiring high local storage density.
description: OVHcloud t1-180 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs with 64 GB of aggregate VRAM. Compute is driven by 36 dedicated Intel Xeon Silver 4214 physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz, coupled with 180.0 GB of RAM, 4050 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 10 Gbps baseline network link. Synthetic testing indicates weak single-threaded CPU capability but average multi-core throughput, while the multi-GPU setup delivers top-tier performance for medium-parameter LLM inference tasks. The integrated NVMe capacity accommodates local datasets without external storage attachments. This configuration is tailored for deep learning training, AI inference, parallel numeric computing, and data-intensive batch workloads where GPU acceleration dominates processing demands.
